q: One room logs CO2 every hour, and one value is 5000 ppm by mistake.
Which summary of the series changes the least?
why: The median only looks at the middle of the sorted values; one extreme value barely moves it.

q: A classifier has precision 0.9 and recall 0.1.
why: F1 = 2 * 0.9 * 0.1 / (0.9 + 0.1) = 0.18. The weaker of the two pulls F1 down.

q: The correlation between two sensors is r = 0.
a: There is no relationship at all
The points lie on a line
One of the sensors is broken
why: r only measures linear relationships; a U-shaped pattern can still give r = 0.

q: Light in a room is low at night and high during the day.
What can a histogram with only 3 bins hide?
why: Wide bins merge separate groups; try it in the histogram example.

q: Half of the readings of a solar inverter are exactly 0 W.
What is the most likely reason?
why: No sun, no power: every night gives a run of zeros. Keep them, but know why they are there.

q: You want to see how temperature and heating power are related.
why: A scatter plot shows every pair of values, so you see the shape of the relationship.
